mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals fewer out-of-home trips and less commuting, which reduces incidental retail visits with a short lag. Over the next four weeks, RETAIL_REC should move lower than the prior four-week mean if these activity losses persist.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not below the prior 28-day mean despite continued low WORKPLACES and TRANSIT levels.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises above its recent average while WORKPLACES falls, trip chaining shifts from commute-linked shopping to at-home staying, depressing discretionary retail visits within one to two weeks. This should push RETAIL_REC lower over the next month.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds t-2w by at least 1 point while WORKPLACES is below t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to fall within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL rises and WORKPLACES remains depressed.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES of more than five points week-on-week indicates tightening mobility constraints or enforcement, which suppresses shopping trips with a near-immediate effect. Under that threshold, RETAIL_REC should decline over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls > 5 points week-on-week and WORKPLACES falls > 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:both series are already below baseline and fell sharply from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain below its prior four-week average after simultaneous large declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: An accelerating decline in PARKS together with weaker RETAIL_REC indicates a broader demand shock, often consistent with adverse weather or seasonal pullback. If PARKS stays well below recent weeks for a full month, retail and recreation mobility should continue downward.
candidate_trigger: PARKS is below t-2w by at least 10 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though PARKS remains far below its recent level.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM with only a mild change in residential behavior indicates demand is being redirected to essential local trips rather than discretionary shopping. If grocery activity rises first, retail recreation should lag and remain weaker over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while RESIDENTIAL changes by less than 1 point
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM increases without a matching residential shift.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both rise while TRANSIT stays depressed, households are substituting toward local leisure and home-based activity instead of retail trips. That substitution should keep RETAIL_REC below its last-month average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day mean despite simultaneous strength in PARKS and RESIDENTIAL with low TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid drop in TRANSIT below the level of the prior two weeks marks a mobility shock that reduces access to shopping corridors. The effect should appear within two weeks and lower RETAIL_REC relative to the previous month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below its t-2w level by more than 3 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after TRANSIT crosses below its t-2w level.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently low WORKPLACES combined with a weaker fall in GROCERY_PHARM implies work-related and errand-based trip generators are both shrinking, which should continue to pull discretionary retail down. This mechanism acts over a four-week horizon and fails if retail stabilizes despite both proxies staying weak.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC returns to or above its prior four-week average while WORKPLACES and GROCERY_PHARM remain below baseline.
